title: Understanding Income Plus Arbitrage Funds: Returns Explained
description: Income plus arbitrage funds combine equity arbitrage strategies with investments in debt instruments. They aim to generate relatively stable, low-volatility r.

faq.a: An arbitrage opportunity arises when the same asset is simultaneously trading at different prices in different markets. Fund managers exploit this by buying in the cheaper market and selling in the more expensive market to lock in a risk-free profit.

faq.q: How are income plus arbitrage funds taxed?
faq.a: These funds are typically taxed as equity-oriented funds if they maintain at least 65% equity exposure. Short-term capital gains (within 1 year) are taxed at 15%, while long-term capital gains (after 1 year) are exempt up to ₹1 lakh per financial year, with gains above this taxed at 10%.

faq.q: Are income plus arbitrage funds risk-free?
faq.a: No, they are not entirely risk-free. While the arbitrage component aims for market-neutral returns, the debt component carries interest rate and credit risk. Opportunities for arbitrage can also fluctuate, impacting returns.

faq.q: What is the typical return expectation from these funds?
faq.a: Returns are generally modest, often in the range of 6-8% annually, aiming to be slightly higher than traditional debt instruments on a post-tax basis, but lower than diversified equity funds.

faq.q: How do they differ from pure debt funds?
faq.a: Pure debt funds invest solely in fixed-income securities and are primarily exposed to interest rate and credit risk. Income plus arbitrage funds combine debt investments with an equity arbitrage strategy, aiming for better tax efficiency and a different risk-return profile.

faq.q: Can Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) invest in these funds?
faq.a: Yes, NRIs can generally invest in income plus arbitrage funds through their NRE or NRO accounts, subject to prevailing regulations. However, their taxation might differ based on their country of residence and DTAA (Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement) provisions.

faq.q: What is the ideal investment horizon for these funds?
faq.a: While suitable for short to medium-term goals (1-3 years) due to their low volatility, their tax efficiency (LTCG benefits) makes them particularly attractive for investment horizons exceeding one year.
